android_mechanism: OUI CSV import commits each row separately; fix batches all inserts into one transaction
bug_description: The dataset-sync page imports the classic-poem dataset by iterating the parsed JSON array and issuing one standalone RDB INSERT per poem (each in its own autocommit transaction, all fired concurrently via a non-awaited map). Importing thousands of rows generates thousands of individual journal/fsync cycles, saturating the DB writer and freezing the sync page for a long time.
fix_summary: Dataset import uses RdbStore.batchInsert so the whole array is inserted in a single transaction; the per-row debug logging is removed.
trigger_steps: Install the app with an empty database; ensure network access to the dataset URL.
Start hitrace capture (categories: app, sched, disk, filesystem).
Open settings -> 数据同步 (sync data) to trigger the dataset fetch and import.
Wait until import completes (row count stable in hilog). Stop hitrace. Repeat 3 repetitions for unfixed (clear app data between repetitions), then install fixed and repeat 3 repetitions.

test_oracle.definition: Time from dataset JSON parse completion to the last INSERT commit observed in disk/database trace activity.
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed: one sqlite journal/fsync cycle per row (thousands of small commits); fixed: single batched commit. unfixed_import_ms > fixed_import_ms by >= 3x for a multi-thousand-row dataset.

trace_config.command: hdc shell hitrace --time 60 app sched disk filesystem database -o /data/local/tmp/jingmo_import.chtrace
